units.text: As outlined in the Secure by Design policy, these principles are mandatory for government departments and arm’s length bodies (ALBs), and optional for other parts of the public sector.
units.text_start: these principles are mandatory for government departments and arm’s length bodies
units.text_end: optional for other parts of the public sector

units.text: The Cyber Security Standard requires all organisations delivering new digital services and technical infrastructure to meet the 10 Secure by Design principles.
units.text_start: requires all organisations delivering new digital services
units.text_end: meet the 10 Secure by Design principles

units.text: The Service Standard Point 9(Create a secure service which protects users’ privacy) advises service teams that they must follow the Secure by Design principles.
units.text_start: they must follow the Secure by Design principles

units.section: 1. Create responsibility for cyber security risk
units.text: Assign risk owners to be accountable for managing cyber security risks for a service throughout its life cycle. These must be senior stakeholders with the experience, knowledge and authority to lead on security activities.
units.text_start: Assign risk owners to be accountable for managing cyber security risks
units.text_end: authority to lead on security activities

units.text: Where third-party products are used, perform security due diligence by continually assessing platforms, software and code for security vulnerabilities.
units.text_start: perform security due diligence by continually assessing platforms

units.section: 5. Build in detect and respond security
units.text: Design for the inevitability of security vulnerabilities and incidents. Integrate appropriate security logging, monitoring, alerting and response capabilities. These must be continually tested and iterated.
units.text_start: Design for the inevitability of security vulnerabilities and incidents

units.text: Implement continuous security assurance processes to create confidence in the effectiveness of security controls, both at the point of delivery and throughout the operational life of the service.
units.text_end: throughout the operational life of the service

units.section: How organisations show they’re implementing Secure by Design
units.text: While Secure by Design is not an assurance process, one of its principles is to continuously deliver effective security controls throughout the life of a service. Delivery teams should complete a self assessment as evidence they’re meeting the Secure by Design principles.
units.text_start: Delivery teams should complete a self assessment
units.text_end: meeting the Secure by Design principles

units.text: Commercial and procurement teams play a vital role in ensuring that cyber security is embedded into government digital and technology procurements from the outset. Secure by Design should be a core consideration throughout the procurement life cycle, from defining requirements and evaluating suppliers to contract management and service delivery.
units.text_start: Secure by Design should be a core consideration throughout the procurement life cycle

units.text: All central government departments and arm's length bodies (ALBs) must incorporate effective security practices and meet the Secure by Design policy when delivering and building digital services and technical infrastructure.
units.text_start: must incorporate effective security practices and meet the Secure by Design policy
